fix: The researcher advises blocking web access to the site's wp-content/upgrade folder before updating. WordPress released the fix last week in version 7.1.4 and in matching updates for older branches back to 4.7, all listed in its security advisory.
impact: An attacker with no account who can determine the folder's name and access the installer before WordPress deletes the copy can end up running code on the server. An attacker who catches the window during that update can still set up the temporary copy of WordPress with their own database, log in to it, and run PHP code with the web server's permissions before the copy is deleted, Bayram says in his technical write-up. From there, the attacker can read or write files in the live WordPress site.

impact: Attackers abused a self-registration feature in the system’s account manager, built for other purposes and not requiring MFA, to create a read-only account that had access to archived data between June 27 and July 2. DigiCert blocked the unauthorized account on July 2, and determined in October that the account was used to access archived customer contact information, including names, email addresses, phone numbers, and business addresses. In some cases, driver’s licenses, passports, utility bills, and other documents containing a name and address that its customers provided were also compromised. “The access could not write records, act as a validation approver, or issue certificates,” DigiCert says. “The CA systems operate on their own secure network segments and were not affected by this external access.” Advertisement.

fix: Take controllers off the internet The agencies want owners and operators to act “immediately,” and the first item on their list is to stop exposing controller panels and other control system devices to the internet. Operators are also told to put operational technology devices on a dedicated VLAN separate from business networks, change default passwords, and turn on phishing-resistant multifactor authentication where feasible. Firmware should be kept up to date, and devices the vendor no longer supports should be retired and replaced.
impact: Once an attacker gets in, the temperature settings can be changed remotely, and a unit forced into heating “can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies wrote. Hundreds of supermarkets in France were left with spoiled stock after attackers remotely hijacked the systems controlling their fridges and freezers overnight and set them to warm their contents. This week, the French Blood Establishment (EFS) confirmed that three of its blood banks detected a temperature spike in their cold rooms after one of its refrigeration equipment providers was hit.
quote: Once an attacker gets in, the temperature settings can be changed remotely, and a unit forced into heating “can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards,” the agencies wrote
